## Bug-Introducing Commits
BIC: aef6f032ea31d1d05104adf8560ca479cd27d8ad

## Reasoning

(1) I traced the full history of `BddRunContext.java`'s `runningBatchKey` field using `git log --follow -p` to see every change to that field across all commits, then inspected each relevant commit's diff in detail.

(2) The field `private Optional<String> runningBatchKey;` was declared with no initializer in the very first commit that created this class (`aef6f032`, Aug 2019). It stayed uninitialized (defaulting to Java's `null`) through every subsequent change, including `c6b7e2d8`, `c9e5d87`, `df5af23`, and `09fa1e43` — none of these touched the declaration itself. The fix commit (`1ea50f5`) finally adds `= Optional.of("batch-1")` to the declaration, with the comment "must be initialized for jbehave-junit-runner" and a regression test asserting the default value is `"batch-1"`. Since `getRunningBatchKey()`/`getRunningBatch()` call `.orElseThrow(...)` or similar `Optional` methods on this field, calling them before `putRunningBatch` was ever invoked (as happens under jbehave-junit-runner, which apparently doesn't call that setter) would throw a `NullPointerException` instead of the expected `IllegalStateException` or default value — this is the bug being fixed.

(3) Evidence: the field has never had an initializer until the fix commit; the fix's own comment explicitly calls out that it "must be initialized," and the added test (`testGetDefaultRunningBatchKey`) exercises exactly the uninitialized-access path. Since the bug is the simple absence of an initializer, the root cause traces to the commit that first introduced the field without one.

I'm fairly confident in this identification — the field was never modified at the declaration site between its creation and the fix, so there's no intermediate candidate commit that could have introduced the missing initialization.
